glossary.definition: The role responsible for decisions and records in the defined workflow.
A point where a record moves from one person or system to another.
Statements the team can test when judging software.
Requirements and internal procedures used as a reference for an audit.
What the auditor saw, read or was told, recorded with enough detail for someone else to check it.
A judgment drawn from observations and measured against criteria.
A statement of what evidence must exist, who checks it and by when.
A record class for material needed in planning or follow-up.
A record class for material worth keeping and searchable, but not used in daily work.
A record class for material kept in its existing location with a pointer from the new system.
A record class for material no longer needed, subject to retention rules.
The point at which the new system becomes the working record.
Deciding in advance what would trigger a rollback and how it would work.
A role-specific exercise using sample records whose result is shown to someone who can judge it.
A test of whether real users can do real work in the system with their records and constraints.
A rollout that brings in groups of users or parts of the program in a planned order.

example.label: Illustrative example
example.description: An unnamed Canadian manufacturer evaluates internal audit management software for one production workflow; all situations and records are hypothetical, not customer results.
